notes: The italic 'many' is added while the 'for' before it is rule 33's supplied word on the bare accusative of duration שָׁנִים; only the adjective is unlicensed.
בְּיַד fuses to 'by' under rule 30, which names this pair explicitly.

'of whom' is kept whole with אֲשֶׁר, headed on the relative pronoun. The defensible alternative is rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, giving the 'of' to דִּבַּרְתִּי as the word by which the English verb reaches its bare object; the accepted reading is preferable because English pied-pipes the preposition with the relative it stands beside.
